stages.a: A pillowy top on the block, dotted with moisture bubbles.
stages.v: Do not rush or disturb incubation. "Spider eyes", moisture bubbles on a pillowy top, show at about 4-6 weeks.

stages.a: Knobbly primordia build up across the top.
stages.v: Primordia build across the top at about 4-8 weeks. Give noticeably more light than usual incubation.

stages.a: The primordia rise toward the patch as a fist, splitting into fingers.
stages.v: At 5-8 weeks the fists split into fingers: time to cut. Check every block; they do not stay in sync.

stages.a: The bag top is cut off above the block, and slits open in the sides.
stages.v: Cut the bag top off, but not down to the block: the rest of the bag is a microclimate. Slit one or two sides so the mushroom can push out and CO2 can spill out.

stages.a: The tops darken and fronds open fast, fan over fan.
stages.v: Healthy blocks show the primordia tops darkening after the cut; fronds then form fast. A block cut too early stalls.

stages.a: A full rosette of grey-brown fronds on branching white stalks.
stages.v: Harvest when the fronds have formed, 7-10 days after the cut. One flush only.

labels.a: Moisture bubbles on the pillowy top.
The knobbly first growths of the fruit body.
labels.v: Too little light shows as brown primordia only around the edge.

labels.a: The rising mass, splitting into fingers.
labels.v: Fist-to-fingers: time to cut. On a scale farm, give staff a ruler mark for the height.

labels.a: The bag top cut off, not down to the block.
labels.v: The remaining bag is a protective microclimate.

labels.a: A slit in the side of the bag.
labels.v: One or two side slits let the mushroom push out and CO2 spill out.
Healthy blocks show the primordia tops darkening considerably after the cut.
Fronds form fast once the tops darken.

labels.a: The underside of each frond is fine pores, not gills.
White stalks branch from one base to carry the fronds.
labels.v: Some buyers want the whole "blob": it slices like king oyster. Others want shredded fronds.
